bmi.label: BMI
bmi.description: Your body mass index is 48.5 kg/m², which falls in the obesity range and raises long-term cardiometabolic and joint-health risk. A balanced diet, steadier routine, and gradual activity increases are the healthiest path to weight management.

scoreSummary.label: Your overall assessment score:
scoreSummary.footnote: *Generated from the FFQ nutrition assessment and four core health dimensions.

dailyGoalSection.title: Daily micro-goal
dailyGoalSection.itemTitle: Switch to a larger water bottle
dailyGoalSection.description: Better hydration supports digestion and metabolic balance. Keeping a bottle you like within reach makes the habit much easier to repeat.

specialRemindersSection.title: Special reminders
items: If you have gout or elevated uric acid, avoid high-purine fish, organ meats, concentrated broths, and alcohol to reduce flare risk.
If you are preparing for pregnancy, consider 400 μg of folic acid daily starting three months before conception and continuing into early pregnancy.
Before pregnancy-focused supplementation, use balanced meals and moderate exercise to move BMI toward a steadier range.
Some long-term anti-inflammatory medicines can increase vitamin C depletion, so extra attention to intake may be helpful.

items.title: Increase naturally iron-rich foods
items.content: If your diet leans plant-based, prioritize grains, beans, nuts, and dark greens, and pair them with vitamin C-rich foods to improve iron absorption.

items.title: Moderate soy intake around ovulation
items.content: If soy foods are heavily concentrated in your diet during ovulation, pull them back slightly and keep meals varied rather than excessive.

items.title: Close vitamin C gaps through food first
items.content: Add oranges, kiwi, peppers, potatoes, and leafy greens more consistently, then use supplements only if food intake stays difficult.

items.title: Keep caffeine within a safe range
items.content: For healthy adults, daily caffeine is best kept below 400 mg, which is roughly equal to two or three medium Americanos.

items.title: Quitting smoking lowers multiple risks
items.content: Smoking strongly increases pulmonary, cardiovascular, and digestive disease risk. The earlier you stop, the greater the long-term benefit.

items.title: Eat deep-sea fish at least three times a week
items.content: Salmon, sardines, and other omega-3-rich fish support lipid balance and cardiovascular health and can be a preferred protein choice.

items.title: Whole fruit beats juice
items.content: Fresh fruit keeps more fiber intact and makes it harder to consume excess free sugar without noticing.

exerciseAdviceSection.title: Movement and recovery

items.title: Aim for at least 150 minutes of activity each week
items.content: Sedentary time increases metabolic and cardiovascular burden. Brisk walking, cycling, and light strength work are practical ways to build a steadier weekly baseline.

exerciseAdviceSection.footnote: *These suggestions combine your goals, nutrition habits, movement, and routine to support a more balanced long-term lifestyle.

closingSection.note: Because health status, habits, and goals change over time, retake the assessment every three months and compare the result with your poster history.

nutritionSection.title: Goal-based nutrition plan
nutritionSection.description: Recommended nutrients based on your current improvement goals

immunity.name: Vitamin C
immunity.benefit: Supports immune-cell activity and helps the body maintain a steadier defense response.

immunity.name: Zinc
immunity.benefit: Supports immune development and repair while helping with tissue recovery and mucosal protection.

immunity.name: Vitamin D3
immunity.benefit: Helps regulate immune responses and also supports calcium absorption and bone health.

gut.name: Probiotics
gut.benefit: Helps balance the gut microbiome and improve bloating, digestion, and bowel comfort.

gut.name: Dietary Fiber
gut.benefit: Supports bowel movement and satiety and is a core part of improving everyday diet quality.

gut.name: L-Glutamine
gut.benefit: Supports gut-lining repair and helps maintain a stronger intestinal barrier.

stress.name: Magnesium
stress.benefit: Supports muscle relaxation, calmer stress response, and better sleep quality.

stress.name: Vitamin B Complex
stress.benefit: Supports the nervous system and energy metabolism and can help reduce fatigue load.

stress.name: Omega-3
stress.benefit: Supports mood steadiness and brain health and is a common baseline nutrient for long-term stress care.
